title: Effective etale descent of fine log schemes with a compatible polarization
statement:
Let $(S,M)$ be a fine log scheme: a log scheme in the sense of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] with etale-local charts by finitely generated integral monoids, without requiring saturation. Let $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective etale covering [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with the pulled-back log structures. Thus these morphisms are strict: the source log structure is the log structure associated to the inverse image of $M$ and its structure map. For every $i$ let $X_i\to U_i$ be a fine log scheme. On $U_{ij}=U_i\times_SU_j$ [def-pc-fibre-product] suppose given log isomorphisms
$$\theta_{ij}:X_i\times_{U_i}U_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}X_j\times_{U_j}U_{ij}$$
over $U_{ij}$, satisfying the identity and cocycle conditions on triple fibre products. Let $L_i$ be an invertible module on the underlying scheme of $X_i$ [def-sc-invertible-module], with isomorphisms $\theta_{ij}^*L_j\simeq L_i$ satisfying the same cocycle conditions. Assume that $L_i$ is relatively ample over $U_i$: for every affine open $V\subseteq U_i$, its restriction to the inverse image of $V$ is ample in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then there exist a fine log scheme $X\to S$, an invertible module $L$ on its underlying scheme, and isomorphisms $(X,L)\times_SU_i\simeq(X_i,L_i)$ inducing all the specified data. The resulting object with these identifications is unique up to unique compatible isomorphism. If all $X_i$ are fs, then $X$ is fs. Moreover, morphisms of fine log schemes are local on the source for the strict etale topology: for any fine log schemes $T,Z$ over $S$, any jointly surjective strict etale covering $\{T_a\to T\}$, and any family of log $S$-morphisms $T_a\to Z$ agreeing on $T_a\times_TT_b$, there is a unique log $S$-morphism $T\to Z$ inducing that family.

source.place: Tag 0D3C (lemma-descending-property-ample), together with spaces.tex Tag 02WW (theorem-presentation) and spaces-descent.tex Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), for effective descent with a relatively ample sheaf. Fine log structures and their morphisms descend as sheaves of monoids on the small etale site; ILO Expose VIII 3.3.8, printed pp. 107--108, invokes this descent for log charts.

proof.text: Forget the log structures and apply [lem-trf-polarized-scheme-etale-descent]. The underlying $\theta_{ij}$ have the identity and cocycle conditions; the specified $\theta_{ij}^*L_j\simeq L_i$ have their own identity and cocycle conditions, so the line-bundle datum meets the corrected child hypothesis. Relative ampleness is exactly ampleness after restriction to every affine open of $U_i$. Obtain $f:X\to S$, an invertible module $L$, and compatible identifications $X\times_SU_i\simeq X_i$ carrying $L$ to $L_i$.

source.place: Tag 0D3C with scheme effectivity through Tags 02WW and 04W8.

proof.text: Under these identifications the maps $p_i:X_i\to X$ are the base changes of $U_i\to S$ along $f$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] makes $\{p_i:X_i\to X\}$ a jointly surjective etale cover of the descended $X$. Each $X_i$ is locally Noetherian, since it is a fine log scheme in the sense of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Apply [lem-trf-etale-local-noetherian-descent] to this cover: $X$ is locally Noetherian. This establishes the underlying-scheme hypothesis of fine-log descent before applying it.

source.place: Tag 034C (lemma-Noetherian-local-fppf); ILO VI 1.1 convention; Morphisms Tag 02GO and Topologies Tag 022D for the base-changed covering.

proof.text: Use the cover $\{X_i\to X\}$ of Step 2. The overlap $X_i\times_XX_j$ identifies with $X\times_SU_{ij}$ by the fibre-product universal property. The log parts of $\theta_{ij}$ therefore identify the restrictions of $M_{X_i}$ and $M_{X_j}$ on precisely these overlaps, over the structure sheaf. Their identity and triple cocycle follow from those of the given log isomorphisms. By [lem-trf-fine-log-structure-etale-descent] they glue to a fine log structure $M_X$ on $X$ with compatible identifications $M_X|_{X_i}\simeq M_{X_i}$.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8 final sentence, printed pp. 107--108; VI 1.1.

proof.text: Construct the log structure map for $f$. Let $A=f^{-1}M_S$, equipped with $f^{-1}M_S\to f^{-1}\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal O_X$, and let $B=M_X$. On $X_i$, the given log morphism $X_i\to U_i$ followed by the strict log morphism $U_i\to S$ gives $A|_{X_i}\to M_{X_i}=B|_{X_i}$. These maps agree on $X_i\times_XX_j$ because $\theta_{ij}$ is a log isomorphism over $U_{ij}$. The arbitrary-monoid-sheaf clause of [lem-trf-fine-log-structure-etale-descent] gives a unique $f^\flat:f^{-1}M_S\to M_X$ compatible with the structure maps. Together with $f$ this is a log morphism by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Its restrictions are the specified log morphisms, so the identifications of Step 1 are now over the log base $S$ and induce the original polarization and overlap data.

source.place: VI 1.1 and VIII 3.3.8: sheaf gluing of the structure morphism to the base, after scheme descent.

proof.text: If every $X_i$ is fs, its log structure has etale-local charts by fine saturated monoids. Apply the saturated-chart clause of [lem-trf-fine-log-structure-etale-descent] to the same cover of $X$. It gives saturated charts for $M_X$, and therefore $X$ is fs.

For two descents $(X,M_X,L)$ and $(X\prime,M_{X\prime},L\prime)$ with the specified identifications, let $h_i:X_i\to X\prime$ be the underlying comparison isomorphisms followed by projection to $X\prime$. They agree on $X_i\times_XX_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale] the cover of Step 2 is fpqc, and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] descends the $h_i$ to a unique $h:X\to X\prime$. Its two composites to $S$ agree on the cover, so uniqueness of that same descent with target $S$ shows $h$ is over $S$. Applying the same argument on $X\prime$ descends the inverse comparisons; the two inverse equations hold globally by uniqueness after restriction. The uniqueness clause of [lem-trf-polarized-scheme-etale-descent] gives the compatible invertible-module isomorphism for this same underlying $h$. The local log comparisons are maps $h^{-1}M_{X\prime}|_{X_i}\to M_X|_{X_i}$. Apply the arbitrary-monoid-sheaf clause of [lem-trf-fine-log-structure-etale-descent] to descend them and their inverse comparisons. Its uniqueness makes their composites identities and makes the resulting log isomorphism commute with the maps from $M_S$, since both assertions hold locally. Every compatible log isomorphism has this underlying scheme map and this monoid-sheaf map by the same two uniqueness assertions. This proves unique compatible isomorphism of the polarized log descents.

source.place: Tag 023Q and Topologies Tag 022C; uniqueness in polarized scheme descent and sheaf-level log descent.

proof.text: For the final assertion write $q_a:T_a\to T$ and $g_a:T_a\to Z$ for the given strict etale cover and compatible log $S$-morphisms. The underlying $g_a$ agree on $T_a\times_TT_b$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale] this is an fpqc cover, so [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] produces a unique scheme map $g:T\to Z$ with $gq_a=g_a$. If $t:T\to S$ and $z:Z\to S$ are the structure maps, then $(zg)q_a=zg_a=tq_a$ for every $a$. The uniqueness in representable descent, now with target $S$, implies $zg=t$; hence the underlying descended map is an $S$-morphism.

Equip $A=g^{-1}M_Z$ with the composite $g^{-1}M_Z\to g^{-1}\mathcal O_Z\to\mathcal O_T$ and put $B=M_T$. Strictness of $q_a$ identifies $M_{T_a}$ with $M_T|_{T_a}$, so the log parts of $g_a$ give maps $u_a:A|_{T_a}\to B|_{T_a}$ over $\mathcal O_{T_a}$. They agree on overlaps because the given $g_a$ agree as log morphisms. Apply the arbitrary-monoid-sheaf clause of [lem-trf-fine-log-structure-etale-descent] on the locally Noetherian scheme $T$: it gives a unique $g^\flat:g^{-1}M_Z\to M_T$ over $\mathcal O_T$. By [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], $(g,g^\flat)$ is a log morphism. It is over the log base $S$: the maps $t^{-1}M_S\to M_T$ obtained from $t$ and from the composite $zg$ agree after every $q_a$, since the $g_a$ are log $S$-morphisms, and the uniqueness in the same sheaf clause makes them equal. The scheme-map uniqueness in Step 7 and the monoid-map uniqueness here give the required uniqueness of the log $S$-morphism.

mathlib_searches.query: Effective etale descent for schemes equipped with compatible relatively ample invertible sheaves and fine logarithmic structures.
